sn10.12:1.2: at one time the Fortunate One was dwelling near Ālavī in the domicile of the yakkha Ālavaka.
sn10.12:1.3: Then the yakkha Ālavaka approached the Fortunate One, and after approaching he said this to the Fortunate One:
sn10.12:1.5: “Yes, friend”, said the Fortunate One, and he got out.
sn10.12:1.7: “Yes, friend”, said the Fortunate One, and he went in.
sn10.12:1.8: For a second time the yakkha Ālavaka said this to the Fortunate One:
sn10.12:1.10: “Yes, friend”, said the Fortunate One, and he got out.
sn10.12:1.12: “Yes, friend”, said the Fortunate One, and he went in.
sn10.12:1.13: For a third time the yakkha Ālavaka said this to the Fortunate One:
sn10.12:1.15: “Yes, friend”, said the Fortunate One, and he got out.
sn10.12:1.17: “Yes, friend”, said the Fortunate One, and he went in.
sn10.12:1.18: For a fourth time the yakkha Ālavaka said this to the Fortunate One:
sn10.12:1.20: “I certainly will not get out, friend,
sn10.12:1.21: so please do whatever it is you must do.”
sn10.12:1.22: “I will ask you a question, ascetic,
sn10.12:1.23: and if you do not answer me, I will overthrow your mind, or split your heart, or seize you by the feet and throw you across the river.”
sn10.12:1.24: “I certainly do not see, friend, in the world with its gods, Māra, and Brahma, in this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, princes and men, anyone who could overthrow my mind, or split my heart, or seize me by the feet and throw me across the river.
sn10.12:1.25: Still, you may ask what you want, friend.”
sn10.12:2.1: “What is the greatest wealth for a person here?
sn10.12:2.2: What, when accomplished, brings about happiness?
sn10.12:2.3: What, for sure, is the sweetest of tastes?
sn10.12:2.4: Living what life do they say is the greatest?”
sn10.12:3.1: “Confidence is a person’s greatest wealth here.
sn10.12:3.2: The Dhamma, when accomplished, brings about happiness.
sn10.12:3.3: Truth, for sure, is the sweetest of tastes.
sn10.12:3.4: Living a wise life they say is the greatest.”
